pages.text: The $(item)Structure Scanner$() captures any build as a reusable blueprint.$(br2)$(li)Right-click the $(l)first corner$() block$(li)Right-click the $(l)opposite corner$() block$(li)Keep a $(item)Blank Blueprint Disc$() $(l)anywhere in your inventory$(), then right-click the air to scan$(br2)The result is a written $(item)Blueprint Disc$(): portable, tradeable, and printable on any machine of the right tier.
Quartz gives the scanner its eyes; glass focuses the lens.
Each craft yields $(l)two$() blank discs. One disc holds one scan.

pages.title: Print, Don't Replace
pages.text: The printer $(l)never overwrites existing blocks$(): it only fills empty space. Clear the print area first, or the printer will skip occupied positions and build the rest.$(br2)Server operators can import WorldEdit $(l).schem$() and Create / vanilla $(l).nbt$() files straight onto discs with $(o)/mc3dprint import$().

pages.title: Scaffolding
pages.text: $(item)Scaffolding$() is how you reach the top corners of a build, so it lands inside most hand scans. The scanner captures it, but the printer acts as if it were not there: it adds $(l)no cost$(), it does $(l)not$() raise the blueprint's tier, and it is $(l)never built$().$(br2)Put it up, scan, tear it down. Without the rule a Tier 1 cottage scanned from a scaffold tower comes back as a $(l)Tier 3$() blueprint needing a machine it never called for.
